correctness.rationale: The four normalized Gaussian coherent vectors have the exact Hermitian Gram entries displayed in the proof. A symbolic determinant identity gives D=[(1-exp(-pi a²))(1-exp(-pi b²))]²-16 exp(-pi(a²+b²))sin⁴(pi ab/2). Rewriting with hyperbolic sines makes D nonnegative and bounds the determinant at the infinite-aspect-ratio boundary, proving existence of maximizers. An exhaustive subsequential analysis of every h_j→0 with a_j≥b_j identifies the limiting ratio: zero if a_j→0 or infinity and pi⁴F(pi a₀²) for finite positive a₀. The analytic Q-derivative chain proves that F has exactly one positive maximum; that yields sharpness and rigidity of all maximizers. The square has leading order pi⁶h⁶/3 by direct expansion. All essential limits, quantifiers and boundary regimes are proved analytically, with symbolic and numerical checker confirmation as a supplement.

originality.rationale: Claim-specific comparison shows that the reviewed four-point HRT theorem concerns dependent shifts for a specially constructed non-Gaussian window, not the Gaussian four-corner Gram volume. Reviewed infinite Gaussian lattice frame-operator bounds optimize a different spectral functional on infinitely many shifts. The published integer-cell four-point linear-independence theorem and the Gaussian-derivative infinite-lattice frame result likewise do not imply any determinant asymptotic or maximizing aspect ratio. value.rationale: For four individually normalized Gaussian coherent atoms, Gram determinant is the squared volume of their joint span, a natural multivariate independence and finite sampling design criterion. The proven sharp constant, universal nonzero long-side scale, exact shape-rigidity theorem and unexpected h⁴ versus square h⁶ separation address a motivated optimization over all eccentricities; this is not a routine fixed-shape Taylor coefficient or arbitrary computational slice. Quantified objective and strict limits prevent overstatement as a global Riesz-bound or infinite-frame theorem.
